setup.input_units: native; encoder units are twice the detents

steps.caption: Patterns 1 and 2 are assigned to channel 1, so channel 1 merges them. Pattern 1 plays scale degrees 1, 3, 5, 7 (C E G B) and pattern 2 plays degrees 3, 5, 7, 1 (E G B C). Note merge is on Average, shown by the dim button at (15,8). Pentatonic snapping of merged notes is off: before you try this, tap K1, open PARAMS > MOSAIC and set Lock merged to pent. to Off. Left On (the default), merged notes snap to the five-note pentatonic version of the scale and you hear different pitches.
steps.title: Starting point

steps.caption: Tap Play (1,8). Each note is the mean of the two patterns' degrees (2, 4, 6, 4): D, F, A, F = MIDI 62, 65, 69, 65. Velocity comes from pattern 1.
steps.title: Average note merging

steps.caption: Tap (15,8) once. The button lights brighter and Note mode on the screen reads UP, which is the manual's Higher: the mean plus the gap between the two degrees.
steps.title: Choose Higher

steps.caption: Tap Play. The notes are F, A, C, E = MIDI 65, 69, 72, 76, wider than either source. Velocity still comes from pattern 1. Use Higher to spread the two lines apart for a wider, brighter contour.
steps.title: Higher note merging

title: Compare Average and Higher note merging
